frozen_R5_priority: Unchanged and not replaced by the PRT newest-origin rule: an active non-Exception primary is never replaced; with no primary or an ordinary primary the FIRST eligible newly arising non-Exception event (close outcome, then its diagnostic, then sweep bookkeeping, in arising order) propagates only after every remaining single attempt; ordinary cleanup errors are latched and returned. _escalates (v5 231-239) is byte-identical to v4; handlers use its allocation-free inline equivalent.

finding_change_map.change: _secondary (unprotected latch.append, lambdas built outside protection) deleted. _secondary_failed sets the preallocated emergency['failed'] flag before a bounded (16) best-effort type-name append inside its own try and never raises. run() preallocates emergency before bootstrap. The bootstrap BaseException handler and _base_exception_line run report, report retention and the compact line each in its own try/except BaseException -> _secondary_failed, cleanup in finally via _cleanup_under. Reader retention under the primary is the single preallocated slot ctx.emergency_reader (no list growth); case-owned retained_exception_readers appends (RD08C/SC33/AD36, normal flow) unchanged. Emergency lines add secondary_failure (the flag).

_Owned: rows carry preallocated close_error/diagnostic_failure keys; _close_once performs the single native close and never raises: on failure it sets the allocation-free owned.uncertain latch and keeps the actual exception on the row BEFORE any repr/list growth, then appends a bounded (16 rows x 200 characters) diagnostic in its own try whose failure sets diagnostics_incomplete and is kept as an event. close() raises only the first eligible non-Exception event (close, then diagnostic) as _escalates allows, or the ordinary close error only without any primary. close_since collects events in arising order, latches and resumes once after a sweep bookkeeping fault (attempted rows skipped, never retried or double-closed), raises the first eligible non-Exception event after every remaining attempt, returns the first event otherwise. _FaultOS: the never-output violations list became the allocation-free flag violated (accounting_ok unchanged whenever no diagnostic failed); records carry cleanup_error; _clear_one performs the identity-checked single close without any diagnostic formatting and never raises; clear_orphans sweeps like close_since. Every exit/refusal decision reads owned.uncertain (bootstrap 1789/1830/1835, finalization 1959/1979), never owned.errors. Direct _Fx finalizers (v5 648-650, 675-677) and the ignored success-path returns in _open_dir/_bootstrap_read (v5 344, 377) are unchanged text but now covered by the latch.

run() preallocates outcome {deadline, budget, error}; _classify maps HarnessDeadlineExceeded/HarnessBudgetExceeded/other Exception. Case emission: one except Exception classifies; deadline/budget keep the v4 stop statuses, any other ordinary failure makes the counted status ERROR (undelivered record); one compact fallback line (case_output_unretained plus emission_failure_type) is attempted in its own try and its failure is classified. Protected-state reads, provisional summary persistence, final close_since(0) and final emission are each classified; _summary_status recomputes phase/exit_code/status from the latched outcome; _code applies one fixed precedence 5 > 6 > 3 > 4 > 0. A run-level except Exception classifies any ordinary failure that escaped every phase handler, cleans up via _cleanup_under (a non-Exception event still propagates per R5), observes the deadline, emits one minimal summary only if none was delivered, observes the deadline again and returns the classified nonzero code. _emit reserves stdout bytes before writing and records summary delivery.

Pre-case refusal: code 5 for HarnessDeadlineExceeded else 7; close_since(0) (a sweep bookkeeping fault latches uncertainty; a non-Exception event still propagates per R5); _late(deadline) after cleanup sets 5; refusal summary in its own try (delivery failure cannot change 7/5; diagnostic bounded to 200 characters; uncertainty flag reported); _late(deadline) after the summary returns 5. No deadline renewal.

implementation_boundaries.timing_hooks: Only PUBLIC reader methods. Census actions are real namespace/link mutations after native census returns. Fresh-reread condition only arms failure injection. No private production ledger access. RD05E's real-clock hook requires an unexpired control deadline at entry and a witnessed transition.
implementation_boundaries.native_identity: Harness proxy records actual dev/ino on native open before any post-call fault. Public report resource selected by bound path/kind/status; numeric ID used only as dynamic relational join to unresolved set. Orphan fd fstat identity checked before one close; original native iterator object kept, never guessed fd.
implementation_boundaries.primary_error: Exact comparison to repr(the actual harness-injected PRIMARY exception) is preservation evidence only. Cleanup error compared by stable harness exception TYPE. No production diagnostic equality, substrings, stage wording or message-based classification.
implementation_boundaries.harness_cleanup: Each retained descriptor gets exactly one close attempt, never retried or double-closed. A failed attempt sets the allocation-free owned.uncertain latch and keeps the exception object on the row before a bounded (16 x 200) best-effort diagnostic; a diagnostic or sweep bookkeeping failure is latched and kept as an event. Frozen R5: an active non-Exception primary is never replaced; otherwise the first eligible non-Exception event propagates after every remaining attempt. A faulting sweep resumes once; two faulting sweeps leave the remaining rows unattempted with the latch set. Proxy orphan cleanup keeps only the allocation-free violated flag and record outcomes. Exit refusal reads latches, never list growth.
implementation_boundaries.emergency: Under an in-flight non-Exception BaseException: reader retention (one preallocated slot), report, report retention, compact line and cleanup are each individually protected; every secondary failure sets the preallocated emergency flag before a bounded best-effort type list and can never replace the primary; the original object propagates.
implementation_boundaries.output_and_exit: One compact case line/deferred row plus summary while the sink accepts them (formats beta-consumer-control-case-v4 / beta-consumer-controls-summary-v4 / beta-negative-controls-run-start-v4); stdout bytes reserved before each write (1 MiB bound holds under failed or partial writes); 20 MiB retained cap. Deadline, budget and ordinary failures in every emission, fallback, finalization and pre-case refusal phase are classified; the exit code follows one precedence 5 > 6 > 3 > 4 > 0 (7 for pre-case refusal unless the deadline is observed crossed), is authoritative and is recomputed after every finalization step; an unavailable sink loses records, never the nonzero classification; an unreadable clock counts as late.
implementation_boundaries.interpreter_boundary: Python frame, iterator, exception and traceback allocation inside the interpreter itself and asynchronous exceptions delivered between protected statements are outside the source guarantee; under allocation failure the interpreter can itself replace an in-flight exception (an ordinary replacement then still yields a classified nonzero exit through the run-level handler). No unbounded-allocation or OOM-completion guarantee is claimed.
